inline_comments.comment: The `beforeEach` block is missing `vi.clearAllMocks()`. Without it, the `logger.warn` spy accumulates call records across tests. The tests named 'returns tsconfig.json when found', 'returns undefined when no tsconfig variant is found', and 'prefers tsconfig.json over fallback variants' all assert `expect(logger.warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. If these run after the fallback tests (which DO trigger the warning), those assertions will spuriously fail because the spy still holds the prior call. Per project spy-mocking convention, add `vi.clearAllMocks()` as the first statement in this `beforeEach`.

Per the project spy-mocking convention, mock behavior (`.mockImplementation(...)`, `.mockReturnValue(...)`) should be configured inside `beforeEach` blocks within nested `describe` groups — never inside individual `test()` bodies, because inline setup can bleed between tests. Each distinct `find.up` scenario here should live in its own nested `describe` block with a dedicated `beforeEach`, e.g. `describe('when tsconfig.json exists', () => { beforeEach(() => { vi.mocked(find.up).mockImplementation(...) }); test(...) })`.

The `'falls back to tsconfig.app.json...'` test only asserts that the warning contains `'tsconfig.app.json'`, but the sibling `'falls back to tsconfig.base.json...'` test also asserts `'No tsconfig.json found'`. For consistency and to fully verify the warning text, the `app.json` test should include both `expect.stringContaining('No tsconfig.json found')` and `expect.stringContaining('tsconfig.app.json')`.

The warning message hardcodes the specific filenames `tsconfig.base.json / tsconfig.app.json`. If `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` in `utils.ts` is ever extended (e.g., to include `tsconfig.vitest.json`), this string won't reflect the change and will silently go stale. Consider a more generic phrasing such as `'No tsconfig file found (tried tsconfig.json, tsconfig.base.json, tsconfig.app.json).'`, or—if these files share a package boundary—derive the list from the exported `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` constant directly.

The fallback chain is duplicated inline here without the `logger.warn` call that `findTsconfigPath` emits when a non-primary tsconfig is used. Users relying on the Vite path-alias resolution path (`TsconfigPaths.loadConfig`) will silently fall back to `tsconfig.base.json` or `tsconfig.app.json` with no indication, while users going through the component manifest path in `reactDocgenTypescript.ts` do get a warning. Adding a `logger.debug` or `logger.warn` when a fallback is picked would make the behavior consistent across both code paths.

Same silent-fallback issue as in `react-docgen.ts`. The inline chain has no warning when `tsconfig.base.json` or `tsconfig.app.json` is used instead of `tsconfig.json`. Webpack loader users get no feedback about the fallback, unlike users of the manifest code path. Additionally, as a separate package from `utils.ts`, any future change to the candidate list or priority order must be manually replicated here, `react-docgen.ts`, and `utils.ts`.

general_comments.comment: The fallback candidate order (`tsconfig.json` → `tsconfig.base.json` → `tsconfig.app.json`) is now defined in three separate places: `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` in `utils.ts`, inline in `react-docgen.ts`, and inline in `react-docgen-loader.ts`. Because the Vite plugin and Webpack loader live in different packages from `utils.ts`, sharing the constant is non-trivial, but the duplication means future changes to the priority order require coordinated updates across all three files. A comment in each inline copy cross-referencing `TSCONFIG_CANDIDATES` would at least make the intentional duplication explicit and help reviewers keep them in sync.

The warning emitted in `utils.ts` (`'No tsconfig.json found. Using "${candidate}" instead...'`) and the warning in `reactDocgenTypescript.ts` (`'No tsconfig.json (or tsconfig.base.json / tsconfig.app.json) found...'`) cover two distinct scenarios: fallback file used vs. no file at all. However, a user who has only `tsconfig.base.json` will see the fallback warning from `findTsconfigPath` (one warning) but not the 'no tsconfig' warning (which fires only when `configPath` is falsy). This behaviour is correct, but the two warning messages use slightly different phrasing for 'no primary tsconfig'. Aligning the introductory clause (e.g. both starting with `'No tsconfig.json found'`) would make it easier to grep logs and understand both warnings come from the same feature.
